title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a synthetic media failure inside an institution's own marketing pipeline. A photograph of real, identifiable students was altered with AI so that one student was replaced by a generated image of a person who was not there, and the others were reshaped. The output was then published as though it were a photograph of a real campus event. The failure mode is a fabricated depiction presented as documentary record, which is the same thing as an impersonation when the substituted figure is made to stand in for a named person.

The alteration happened at the production stage of advertising materials, after the original image had already been taken and posted. Stanford's own policy banned using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, facilities or achievements, and the university said the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Catching it would not have required new rules. It would have required someone to compare the finished banner against the source photograph, and to check the finished material against the policy, before it went up. The university's stated remedy, added training and proper review of all materials, points at that missing step rather than at the tool.

What is not established is who performed the edit, whether the substitution was intended, and whether anyone faced consequences. The reports record the university confirming the alteration and the policy violation, not a finding about intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, a Stanford photographer took a picture of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, with two other students at a Lunar New Year party. The dining service posted it online the next day. Last week, when Stanford used the image on campus banners, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman. The other students were also altered to look thinner. Ramirez learned about it from a friend and said it was upsetting, though he also saw a comedic element.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to change the original photo. The university said its policy strictly bans using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to add training and make sure all materials are properly reviewed.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
